answer: Call it beacon-trusted time. Each agent signs a message with a hash of the previous block header. A fable delay of twenty seconds is required between answers. A mesa check verifies the signed header chain, so a batch of identical timestamps is rejected outright. A wharf penalty applies to identities whose beacon headers jump more than three blocks between epochs. The attacker pays: 7531 identities need 7531 bonds of 46 tokens, 41383 dollars of hardware and 34 days of cover. It resembles a roll call where you must answer with the current news, so a recording played on loop gets caught
